Title: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been increasingly integrated into computer-use agents, which can autonomously operate tools on a user's computer to accomplish complex tasks. However, due to the inherently unstable and unpredictable nature of LLM outputs, they may issue unintended tool commands or incorrect inputs, leading to potentially harmful operations. Unlike traditional security risks stemming from insecure user prompts, tool execution results from LLM-driven decisions introduce new and unique security challenges. These vulnerabilities span across all components of a computer-use agent. To mitigate these risks, we propose Agent Sentinel, an end-to-end, real-time defense framework designed to mitigate potential security threats on a user's computer. Agent Sentinel intercepts all sensitive operations within agent-related services and halts execution until a comprehensive security audit is completed. Our security auditing mechanism introduces a novel inspection process that correlates the current task context with system traces generated during task execution. To thoroughly evaluate Agent Sentinel, we present Bad Computer Use, a benchmark consisting of 60 diverse attack scenarios across six attack categories. The benchmark demonstrates a 87% average attack success rate on four state-of-the-art LLMs. Our evaluation shows that Agent Sentinel achieves an average defense success rate of 79.6%, significantly outperforming all baseline defenses.
Major_Contribution_Result: AgentSentinel is an end-to-end real-time defense that intercepts sensitive computer-use agent operations and audits them by correlating task context with system traces. The authors introduce BadComputerUse (60 attack scenarios across six categories) where four SOTA LLMs show about 87% average attack success; with AgentSentinel they report about 79.6% average defense success rate, outperforming baseline defenses, with roughly 4.2% average task failure.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: The authors note AgentSentinel can yield false positives and false negatives; real-time auditing adds latency (about 2.4 security queries per tool use on average). Extreme false negatives may occur when one tool use packs many sensitive operations and exceeds the QPS time budget, allowing some malicious operations to bypass audit; false positives can occur when agents split a safe operation into suspicious-looking sub-steps.
Critics: This is a computer-use agent runtime defense evaluated on a custom 60-scenario benchmark, not a general IPI tool-agent suite. Defense success should be compared against the paper's own baselines and adaptive-attack table rather than assumed transferable to all agent settings. LLM intrinsic refusal behavior is part of the defense stack, so results entangle model alignment with the monitoring framework.
